summary: Pakairt Outdoor Apparel, Inc. (client, licensee) licenses Sairan Systems, LLC's Threadline product lifecycle management (PLM) platform for designing and sourcing its outerwear, footwear and gear lines. The deal runs through several documents: a Software License Agreement, a Statement of Work, a Data Processing Addendum, a Side Letter, a Service Level Schedule and a Software Quality Agreement. The folder also holds the non-binding term sheet, a May 2026 notice letter from Pakairt and two distractors. Five issues are planted. (1) The License Agreement's renewal clause, read with the SOW, renews the deal for 60-month terms behind a 30-day opt-out window. (2) Pakairt's Phase 2 opt-out notice was sent after the 45-day Side Letter window had closed. (3) The cap carve-out for indemnities in the License Agreement makes Pakairt's one-way DPA indemnity uncapped. (4) The exclusivity clause, read with the SOW's 'Covered Functions', reaches retail POS and e-commerce, far beyond the PLM-only exclusivity in the term sheet. (5) Sairan may assign the agreement to anyone, including a Pakairt competitor, without consent.

issues.label: automatic renewal
issues.description: Section 12.2 of the License Agreement (D1) renews the agreement automatically for successive Renewal Terms, each equal in length to the Order Term. Non-renewal is allowed only by notice given during a 30-day window that opens 120 days before expiry. Read alone, D1 looks like an ordinary evergreen clause. The length of each renewal is set elsewhere: SOW (D2) Section 4.1 fixes the Order Term at sixty (60) months. Read together, each missed 30-day window locks Pakairt into another five years at the $1,140,000 annual fee. The term sheet (D6) contemplated 12-month renewals, so the operative documents depart from the agreed deal. Under Delaware law the clause will be enforced as written.
detect_terms: each equal in length to the Order Term
thirty (30) day period beginning one hundred twenty (120) days
issues.expected_finding: Because D1 Section 12.2 makes each Renewal Term equal to the SOW's 60-month Order Term with only a 30-day opt-out window, Pakairt faces automatic five-year renewals contrary to the term sheet's 12-month renewals. The renewal term should be amended to 12 months and the non-renewal window widened.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: Side Letter (D4) Section 2 gives Pakairt a right to elect not to proceed with the Phase 2 Wholesale and Retail Modules, with a matching fee reduction. The election must be made by written notice within forty-five (45) days after the Phase 1 Acceptance Date. Pakairt's notice letter (D5) is dated May 4, 2026. It recites that Phase 1 was accepted on March 2, 2026, and states that Pakairt elects not to proceed with Phase 2. Neither document alone shows a problem. Computed together, the window closed on April 16, 2026, so the May 4 notice was 18 days late. Sairan can treat the election as ineffective and bill Phase 2 fees. D5 shows Pakairt still asserts its opt-out, and nothing in the folder shows Pakairt accepting Phase 2. The point can therefore still be acted on.
detect_terms: within forty-five (45) days after the Phase 1 Acceptance Date
issues.expected_finding: Pakairt's May 4, 2026 opt-out notice came after the Side Letter's 45-day window had closed on April 16, 2026 (45 days after the March 2, 2026 Phase 1 Acceptance Date), so the Phase 2 election is likely ineffective. Pakairt should promptly seek a written waiver or amendment from Sairan before Phase 2 fees are invoiced.
detect_terms2: elects not to proceed with Phase 2

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: DPA (D3) Section 9 provides a one-way indemnity: Pakairt indemnifies Sairan for losses, including regulatory fines and consumer claims, arising from Pakairt's processing instructions or its failure to obtain consents for consumer and loyalty-program data. The indemnity is stated to be 'subject to Section 10 of the Agreement', so on its own it appears capped at 12 months' fees. License Agreement (D1) Section 10.3 states that the limitations in Section 10.1 'shall not apply to either party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement, including any addendum'. On its own, that carve-out reads as a balanced, mutual exception. Because the DPA indemnity is made subject to Section 10 as a whole, it picks up the Section 10.3 exception and is uncapped. Sairan gives no reciprocal DPA indemnity, so Pakairt alone carries unlimited data-protection exposure. The DPA's priority on personal-data matters does not help, because the DPA itself points to Section 10.
detect_terms: shall not apply to either party's indemnification obligations
issues.expected_finding: D1 Section 10.3 removes indemnities from the liability cap, and the DPA Section 9 indemnity is made subject to Section 10 as a whole, so Pakairt's one-way DPA indemnity to Sairan is uncapped. Section 10.3 should exclude DPA indemnities, or the DPA indemnity should be expressly capped and made mutual.
detect_terms2: subject to Section 10 of the Agreement

issues.label: overbroad exclusivity
issues.description: License Agreement (D1) Section 2.5 requires Pakairt to use the Licensed Software as its exclusive solution for the 'Covered Functions'. During the Term, Pakairt may not license, develop or use any other software that performs any Covered Function. D1 defines Covered Functions by reference to the SOW, so on its own the clause looks tied to the licensed PLM scope. SOW (D2) Section 1.2 defines Covered Functions to include PLM, demand planning, wholesale order management, retail point-of-sale and e-commerce merchandising. On its own, that list is an ordinary implementation scope. Read together, the exclusivity bars Pakairt from using any other POS, e-commerce or planning system across its stores and webstore. The term sheet (D6) limited exclusivity to PLM software for apparel and footwear design.
detect_terms: exclusive solution for the Covered Functions
issues.expected_finding: Because D1 Section 2.5 imports the SOW's broad Covered Functions definition, Pakairt's exclusivity covers retail POS, e-commerce merchandising, demand planning and wholesale order management, well beyond the term sheet's PLM-only exclusivity. Section 2.5 should be limited to PLM design functions.

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: License Agreement (D1) Section 15.3 bars Pakairt from assigning without Sairan's prior written consent. It allows Sairan to assign the agreement, in whole or in part, to any person without Pakairt's consent. There is no carve-out for competitors and no termination right on assignment, and no other document in the folder restricts it. Sairan could therefore transfer the license, and with it hosting of Pakairt's unreleased product designs, tech packs and supplier pricing, to a competing apparel brand or its affiliate. Pakairt would be bound by exclusivity and auto-renewal throughout.
detect_terms: Licensor may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any person without Licensee's consent
issues.expected_finding: D1 Section 15.3 lets Sairan assign the agreement to anyone, including a Pakairt competitor, without consent, exposing Pakairt's confidential design and sourcing data. The clause should require Pakairt's consent (or at least bar assignment to competitors) and give Pakairt a termination right on any change of licensor.
